title: A Self is bounded by a cognitive light cone of events it can measure and affect

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A Self is bounded by a cognitive light cone of events it can measure and affect

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Any Self (agent) is demarcated by a computational surface, the spatio-temporal boundary of the events it can measure, model and try to affect; this surface is a cognitive "light cone" that sets the scale and limits of its cognition and allows agents of very different material make-up to be compared.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Any Self is demarcated by a computational surface – the spatio-temporal boundary of events that it can measure, model, and try to affect. This surface sets a functional boundary - a cognitive “light cone” which defines the scale and limits of its cognition.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Abstract”. Scope: All agents: biological, artificial and exobiological

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-01: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.09

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is chiefly a proposed definition for comparing agents. Measurements can instantiate the definition, but they cannot discriminate it from rival definitions of individuality without additional empirical consequences.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The statement could be adopted as a definition and used to map measured sensing and action ranges, but no observation can establish that this particular boundary is the uniquely correct demarcation of a Self.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Alternative agent boundaries can fit the same behavior.

Self and cognitive light cone are stipulated constructs.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The abstract offers a demarcation rule for agents of any substrate. Once 'measure, model, and try to affect' is granted as the definition, every system with some sensors and effectors satisfies it by construction. Datasets of behavior or physiology can fill in a range and cannot decide whether that range is a Self. The claim has no distinct empirical consequence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The sentence defines a Self as the boundary of events it can measure and affect. Any measured sensorimotor range can be labeled a cognitive light cone, and a rival definition of agency can be given the same measurements.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No observation separates this boundary from a non-cognitive description of the same sensors and effectors.

The claim is a definition of Self.
